addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-cleaner: Use this agent after writing or changing C/C++ code, to bring it inside the complexity + coverage budget and prove it with real measurements. It builds with --coverage, runs the tests, scores every function you touched with CRAP = CC^2*(1-coverage)^3 + CC alongside cognitive complexity, then fixes what is over budget by adding the missing tests or splitting a genuinely tangled function - and reports the before/after numbers. Delegate to it whenever you have just written a non-trivial C/C++ function, whenever the user mentions complexity, cyclomatic or cognitive complexity, CRAP, code coverage, gcov, 'make this testable' or 'clean this up', and whenever a CRAP/coverage gate has to pass before work counts as done. Its whole build-and-measure loop is noisy, so running it here keeps that noise out of the main conversation.

Examples:

- assistant: *writes a new parser in src/config.cpp*
  assistant: "Now let me hand this to the code-cleaner agent to measure it and close any coverage gaps"

- user: "is dispatch_event getting too complicated?"
  assistant: "I'll use the code-cleaner agent to measure it rather than guess" (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

---
name: gitea-issue-tracker
description: andesim tickets are Gitea issues at gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim; use the `tea` CLI (login "andes") with --repo nick/hybrid_sim and --description, not --body.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

"Ticket" for the andesim repo means a **Gitea issue** on the origin remote
`https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim`. There is no in-repo ticket
directory and no `.gitea/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`; the tracker was empty until
2026-09-06.

Use the **`tea` CLI** (`~/.local/bin/tea`, v0.15.1, installed 2026-09-06).
The login is already configured under the name `andes` (created from the
`~/.git-credentials` password; tea minted its own access token on the server).

```sh
tea issues create --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim \
  --title "..." --description "$BODY"
tea issues list --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim
```

Two gotchas, both cost a retry:

- The body flag is **`--description` / `-d`**, NOT `--body`.
- **`--repo nick/hybrid_sim` is required.** Auto-detection from the local git
  remote fails ("remote repository required") because the origin URL carries
  userinfo: `https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git`.

The repo has **no labels and no milestones defined**, so don't pass
`--labels`/`--milestone` until some are created. Bodies render GitHub-flavored
markdown (tables work).

Roadmap item IDs (`U10h`, `U11`, `FR-109`, ...) from the `ROADMAP_*.md` files
are the natural ticket titles — see [[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]].
---REMOTE---
origin	https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git (fetch)
origin	https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git (push)

# #19 release: ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is the only supported engine, and S/U        
  privilege must be validated on it (open)                                    
                                                                              
  @nick created 2026-09-08 10:07                                              
                                                                              
  ## Problem                                                                  
                                                                              
  AndeSim v0.1.0 delivers exactly one cycle-accurate engine: ax46mpv_fpga_l3  
  (VLEN 1024, DLEN 1024, ELEN 64, 2 MB L3, built with three privilege levels).
  Every other engine is deferred to a later release and will not be present in
  a v0.1.0 install.                                                           
                                                                              
  Two things assume a different engine, ax45mpv_premium, which will not be    
  there:                                                                      
                                                                              
  • the environment check (andesim doctor) treats the absence of the          
  ax45mpv_premium engine binary as a **hard failure**, so the very first      
  command a new user is told to run reports an error on a correct install     
  • the end-to-end test runner picks ax45mpv_premium as its default engine, so
  the suite cannot run at all on a v0.1.0 install                             
                                                                              
  Separately, the two S/U-privilege handoff fixtures — the supervisor-mode one
  and the user-mode one — are pinned to yet another engine, ax66_makatau,     
  paired with the QEMU CPU model andes-ax66. ax66_makatau is not part of      
  v0.1.0 either, so privilege support would ship unverified.                  
                                                                              
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is also built with three privilege levels, and QEMU offers a
  matching andes-ax46mpv CPU model, so the privilege behaviour can and must be
  validated there instead.                                                    
                                                                              
  ## Required Behavior                                                        
                                                                              
  • **The environment check must report success on an install whose only      
  cycle-accurate engine is **ax46mpv_fpga_l3**.** It must not fail, and must  
  not warn, about the absence of any other engine.                            
  • **The end-to-end test suite must run against **ax46mpv_fpga_l3** when no  
  engine is named.**                                                          
  • **The S/U-privilege handoff must be exercised against **ax46mpv_fpga_l3** 
  paired with the QEMU CPU model **andes-ax46mpv**, and must pass.** Both the 
  supervisor-mode fixture and the user-mode fixture must pass on that pairing.
  If a privilege transport defect is uncovered by moving to this engine,      
  fixing it is part of this work — shipping the fixtures disabled or marked as
  expected failures does not satisfy this ticket.                             
  • Naming an engine explicitly must continue to work. This ticket changes    
  what the default and the environment check expect; it does not require      
  removing the ability to run another engine that happens to be installed.    
                                                                              
  ## Acceptance Scenarios                                                     
                                                                              
    Feature: ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is the supported engine for v0.1.0               
                                                                              
    Scenario: Environment check passes on a single-engine install             
      Given an install whose only cycle-accurate engine is "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"  
      When I run the environment check                                        
      Then it reports success                                                 
      And it does not report a failure or a warning about any absent engine   
                                                                              
    Scenario: The test suite defaults to the supported engine                 
      Given an install whose only cycle-accurate engine is "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"  
      When I run the end-to-end test suite without naming an engine           
      Then the suite runs against "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"                           
      And the suite passes                                                    
                                                                              
    Scenario Outline: Privilege handoff is validated on the supported engine  
      Given the cycle-accurate engine "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"                       
      And the functional engine configured with QEMU CPU model "andes-ax46mpv"
      When I run the <fixture> privilege handoff fixture in hybrid mode       
      Then the run completes successfully                                     
      And the fixture reports the expected result                             
                                                                              
    Examples:                                                                 
      | fixture          |                                                    
      | supervisor-mode  |                                                    
      | user-mode        |                                                    
                                                                              
  ## Compatibility and Constraints                                            
                                                                              
  • The engine pairing for privilege runs is fixed: the cycle-accurate engine 
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3 with the functional engine running the QEMU CPU model andes-
  ax46mpv. Both halves are required; a privilege handoff needs an S/U-capable 
  core on both legs.                                                          
  • Everything already supported must continue to work on this engine: the    
  fast, cycle, and hybrid modes; the marker and PC triggers; the profile      
  command; the bare-metal runtime; the Linux runtime; and state verification. 
                                                                              
  ## QA Procedure                                                             
                                                                              
  1. Prepare an install whose only cycle-accurate engine binary is            
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3. Remove or hide every other engine binary.                  
  2. Run the environment check. Confirm it reports success and says nothing   
  about missing engines.                                                      
  3. List the available engines. Confirm ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is offered and is the
  one selected when none is named.                                            
  4. Run the end-to-end test suite with no engine named. Confirm it runs      
  against ax46mpv_fpga_l3 and passes.                                         
  5. Run the supervisor-mode privilege handoff fixture in hybrid mode, with   
  the functional leg using QEMU CPU model andes-ax46mpv. Confirm it completes 
  and reports the expected result.                                            
  6. Repeat step 5 with the user-mode privilege fixture.

我讀完 #19 了。它跟 vsim 的 build config 沒關係 —— 真正的問題在 **andesim 這邊寫死了 `ax45mpv_premium`**。

## 為什麼不是「改 vsim config 就好」

如果 vsim 只 build `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`，andesim 這三個地方會壞：

| 位置 | 現在的行為 |
|---|---|
| `driver/cmd_doctor.cpp:63` | 找不到 `sim_ax45mpv_premium` → `doctor` 印 **FAIL**（新使用者第一個指令就看到錯誤） |
| `scripts/run_e2e.sh:56` | 預設 `VSIM_BIN=sim_ax45mpv_premium` → 整個 e2e suite 跑不起來 |
| `tests/lib/paths.sh:28` | 同上，contract test 也一樣 |

所以 #19 的前兩條 = 把這些預設改成 `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`。這部分就是你說的「改一下就好」，沒有爭議。

## 「驗證」指的只有一件事

`run_e2e.sh:127-128` 這兩個 fixture 被釘在**另一顆** engine：

```
rt_priv_smode | VSIM_BIN=.../sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128
rt_priv_umode | VSIM_BIN=.../sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128
```

`ax66_makatau` 在 v0.1.0 也不會存在。原本的 ticket 說「那就搬到 ax46mpv_fpga_l3 上驗證，如果搬過去壞了就要修」—— 這才是「驗證」的來源。

## 你說 S/U 暫時不支援 → 範圍變小

那第三條就不做了。改成：

1. `doctor` 預設 engine → `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`（且缺其他 engine 不 FAIL、不 warn）
2. `run_e2e.sh` / `tests/lib/paths.sh` 預設 → `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`
3. `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` 從預設 suite 移除，v0.1.0 文件寫明 **S/U 不支援**（只支援 M-mode handoff）

要我把 #19 改寫成這個範圍嗎？（把 S/U 驗證那段和它的 acceptance scenario 拿掉，換成「S/U deferred」）

兩顆都留的話，#19 就縮得更小了 —— doctor 和 e2e 預設本來就是 `ax45mpv_premium`，那兩條需求直接消失。 現有 binary 都在（8/7 build 的），所以**不需要重跑 Docker build**，只要把 vsim 的 `config.yaml` 收斂成這兩顆，以後 build 就只出這兩個。 ## 剩下要改的（因為其他 engine 會消失） | 檔案 | 現在 | 要變成 | |---|---|---| | `vsim_andesim/config.yaml` | 7 顆 cpu | 只留 `ax45mpv_premium` + `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` | | `scripts/run_e2e.sh:127-128` | `rt_priv_smode/umode` 綁 `sim_ax66_makatau` | 移除（S/U 暫時不支援） | | `tests/vplat/test_vplat_window.sh:35`
`test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh:35` | loop `premium ax46mpv_advanced ax66_makatau` | loop `premium ax46mpv_fpga_l3` | | `tests/vsim/test_vsim_lm_load.sh:71`
`test_vsim_hvm_load.sh:66`
`tests/andes_sim/..._hvm_wiring.sh:70` | 拿 `sim_ax46mpv_advanced` 當「wrapper 沒 backdoor」的反例 | 換成 `sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3`（同一個 wrapper，反例仍成立） | | `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | — | 寫明支援 2 顆 engine、S/U 不支援 | `list engines` 是掃 `sim_*` 自動發現的，不是寫死清單，所以少幾顆 engine 不會壞。 要我現在動手嗎？順序是：先改 vsim `config.yaml` → 改 andesim 的 test/script → 跑 `scripts/test_all.sh` → 最後把 #19 改寫成「S/U deferred + engine set = 2 顆」。

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The uncached syscall-window protocol must work on every host: all vsim
# engines AND QEMU's andes_ae350 mirror. The fixture speaks the raw window
# (u64 MMIO only, no cacheable RAM in the exchange), so a pass here proves
# syscall coherence by construction -- including on ax66_makatau, whose

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'window ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing 'window ok': $out"
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0 (output: $out)"
  echo "[ok] $label: window ok, clean exit"
}

   2 # Sourced (not executed). Provides:
   3 #   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
   4 #   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,

   6 #                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
   7 #                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
   8 #                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
   9 #   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
  10 #                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
  11 #                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
  12 #                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
  13 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG ARGS [QEMU_ARGS...] - spawn QEMU for a plugin-only
  14 #                               drain test (boots $VSIM_ELF with the plugin
  15 #                               attached); sets RC to QEMU's exit code.
  16 
  17 TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  18 TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  19 
  20 if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  21   . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
  22 fi
  23 
  24 hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  25   # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  26   # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  27   # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  28   VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  29   VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  30   VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  31   VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  32   for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
  33     if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
  34       echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
  35       exit 77
  36     fi
  37   done
  38 }
  39 
  40 # Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
  41 # $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
  42 # absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
  43 hybrid_describe_int() {
  44   "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
  45     | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
  46 }
  47 
  48 # Spawn QEMU for a plugin-only drain test: boot $VSIM_ELF on andes_ae350 with
  49 # the hybrid plugin attached, stdin detached, combined output to LOG.
  50 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG PLUGIN_ARGS [EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS...]
  51 # PLUGIN_ARGS is the plugin argument string after "$VSIM_PLUGIN," (e.g.
  52 # "outfile=$STATE"). Sets RC to QEMU's exit code -- deliberately not local,
  53 # callers gate on it -- and toggles errexit off around the spawn exactly like
  54 # every call site used to. No shared-memory backend: plugin-only tests have
  55 # no vsim leg, so nothing else ever opens the mmap, and the machine's default
  56 # RAM is the same 128 MiB the backend used to force.
  57 plugin_qemu_drain() {
  58   local log="$1" plugin_args="$2"; shift 2
  59   set +e
  60   "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  61     -machine andes_ae350 \
  62     -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  63     -nographic \
  64     -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  65     -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  66     "$@" \
  67     -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$plugin_args" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1
  68   RC=$?
  69   set -e
  70 }

  73 # the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
  74 put_word_le() {
  75   local v=$3 bytes="" i
  76   for i in 0 8 16 24; do
  77     bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  78   done
  79   # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  80   printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
  81 }

   6 #                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
   7 #                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
   8 #                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
   9 #   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
  10 #                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
  11 #                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
  12 #                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
  13 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG ARGS [QEMU_ARGS...] - spawn QEMU for a plugin-only
  14 #                               drain test (boots $VSIM_ELF with the plugin
  15 #                               attached); sets RC to QEMU's exit code.
  16 
  17 TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  18 TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  19 
  20 if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  21   . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
  22 fi
  23 
  24 hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  25   # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  26   # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  27   # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  28   VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  29   VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  30   VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  31   VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  32   for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
  33     if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
  34       echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
  35       exit 77
  36     fi
  37   done
  38 }
  39 
  40 # Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
  41 # $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
  42 # absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
  43 hybrid_describe_int() {
  44   "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
  45     | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
  46 }
  47 
  48 # Spawn QEMU for a plugin-only drain test: boot $VSIM_ELF on andes_ae350 with
  49 # the hybrid plugin attached, stdin detached, combined output to LOG.
  50 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG PLUGIN_ARGS [EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS...]
  51 # PLUGIN_ARGS is the plugin argument string after "$VSIM_PLUGIN," (e.g.
  52 # "outfile=$STATE"). Sets RC to QEMU's exit code -- deliberately not local,
  53 # callers gate on it -- and toggles errexit off around the spawn exactly like
  54 # every call site used to. No shared-memory backend: plugin-only tests have
  55 # no vsim leg, so nothing else ever opens the mmap, and the machine's default
  56 # RAM is the same 128 MiB the backend used to force.
  57 plugin_qemu_drain() {
  58   local log="$1" plugin_args="$2"; shift 2
  59   set +e
  60   "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  61     -machine andes_ae350 \
  62     -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  63     -nographic \
  64     -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  65     -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  66     "$@" \
  67     -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$plugin_args" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1
  68   RC=$?
  69   set -e
  70 }
  71 
  72 # Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
  73 # the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
  74 put_word_le() {
  75   local v=$3 bytes="" i
  76   for i in 0 8 16 24; do
  77     bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  78   done
  79   # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  80   printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
  81 }

  72 if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then

  74      || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ]; then

  76     exit 1
  77   fi
  78 fi

# Shared status printers + config/path resolution for test scripts.
# Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#   cfg_val KEY            -> KEY's value from the repo-root config.env
#   vsim_bin_dir           -> external vsim build dir (env, then config.env)
#   qemu_bin               -> path to qemu-system-riscv64, same
#                             env-then-config.env resolution
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release surface: v0.1.0 ships exactly the cycle-accurate engines named by
# shipped_cycle_engines() (lib/log.sh), because the vsim side builds only
# those. Two ways that promise rots:
#
#   1. a test pins an engine that is not shipped -- it then hard-fails (or
#      silently skips, which is worse) on a correct v0.1.0 install. This is
#      exactly what happened to the S/U privilege fixtures, pinned to
#      ax66_makatau.
#   2. a shipped engine is missing from the build dir -- the suite cannot run.
#
# Both are checked statically here, so a wrong engine reference is caught in a
# 1-second contract test instead of a 5-minute e2e timeout.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. No harness script may NAME a deferred engine in code. Full-line comments
#    are stripped first: prose that explains why an engine is deferred (and
#    which one) is documentation, not a dependency.
pat=$(deferred_cycle_engines | tr ' ' '\n' | grep . | paste -sd'|')
hits=""
while IFS= read -r f; do
  h=$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$f" | grep -nE "(${pat})" | sed "s|^|${f#$ROOT/}: |")
  [ -n "$h" ] && hits+="$h"$'\n'
done < <(find "$ROOT/tests" "$ROOT/scripts" -name '*.sh' -type f | sort)
if [ -n "${hits%$'\n'}" ]; then
  fail "harness scripts pin engines v0.1.0 does not ship:"$'\n'"${hits%$'\n'}"
fi
ok "no harness script pins a deferred engine"

# 2. Every shipped engine is present and self-describes as cycle-accurate.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
[ -n "$BINDIR" ] || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR unset and absent from config.env"
for eng in $(shipped_cycle_engines); do
  SIM="$BINDIR/sim_$eng"
  [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "shipped engine missing: $SIM (source ./setup.sh)"
  "$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"kind": *"cycle-accurate"' \
    || fail "$eng --describe does not report kind cycle-accurate"
  ok "shipped engine present: sim_$eng"
done

echo "PASS[andes_sim_engine_set]"
SH
chmod +x tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh; bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh

import sys

def edit(path, subs):
    s=open(path).read()
    for old,new in subs:
        n=s.count(old)
        if n!=1: sys.exit(f'{path}: {n} matches for:\n{old[:200]}')
        s=s.replace(old,new)
    open(path,'w').write(s)
    print('ok', path)

edit('tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh', [(
'''done < <(find "$ROOT/tests" "$ROOT/scripts" -name '*.sh' -type f | sort)''',
'''done < <(find "$ROOT/tests" "$ROOT/scripts" -name '*.sh' -type f \\
           ! -name 'log.sh' | sort)   # log.sh DEFINES the deferred list''')])

# --- 2. vplat engine loops -> the shipped set ---
loop_old = 'for eng in ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_advanced ax66_makatau; do'
loop_new = 'for eng in $(shipped_cycle_engines); do'
edit('tests/vplat/test_vplat_window.sh', [
 ('''# The uncached syscall-window protocol must work on every host: all vsim
# engines AND QEMU's andes_ae350 mirror. The fixture speaks the raw window
# (u64 MMIO only, no cacheable RAM in the exchange), so a pass here proves
# syscall coherence by construction -- including on ax66_makatau, whose
# private write-back PL2C shadows the legacy RAM-magicmem protocol.''',
  '''# The uncached syscall-window protocol must work on every host: every SHIPPED
# vsim engine (shipped_cycle_engines) AND QEMU's andes_ae350 mirror. The
# fixture speaks the raw window (u64 MMIO only, no cacheable RAM in the
# exchange), so a pass here proves syscall coherence by construction. The
# design was forced by ax66_makatau, whose private write-back PL2C shadowed
# the legacy RAM-magicmem protocol; that engine is deferred past v0.1.0 but
# the raw-window contract it exposed is what this test guards.'''),
 (loop_old, loop_new),
 ('ok "window protocol succeeds on every vsim engine + fast"',
  'ok "window protocol succeeds on every shipped vsim engine + fast"')])
edit('tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh', [
 ('''# gettimeofday() must succeed on every vsim engine, not just the default.
# ax66_makatau's mmsc_cfg reports PL2C (L2 cache) support even though its
# build has zero L2 KB configured; vplat_syscalls.c's flush_dcache(), run
# before every HTIF syscall, must not treat that as "safe to touch the L2
# MMIO window" -- gettimeofday is the runtime's first syscall, so a bad
# probe there fails before the ROI even starts.''',
  '''# gettimeofday() must succeed on every SHIPPED vsim engine
# (shipped_cycle_engines), not just the default. The invariant came from
# ax66_makatau, whose mmsc_cfg reported PL2C (L2 cache) support even though
# its build had zero L2 KB configured: vplat_syscalls.c's flush_dcache(), run
# before every HTIF syscall, must not treat an advertised L2 as "safe to touch
# the L2 MMIO window". gettimeofday is the runtime's first syscall, so a bad
# probe there fails before the ROI even starts. ax66_makatau is deferred past
# v0.1.0; the probe contract stays.'''),
 (loop_old, loop_new),
 ('ok "gettimeofday.elf succeeds on every vsim engine + fast"',
  'ok "gettimeofday.elf succeeds on every shipped vsim engine + fast"')])

# --- 3. the stale "ax46 wrapper has no backdoor -> describe 0" blocks. The
# ax46 wrapper GAINED the set_/get_ pair, so the assertion has been failing;
# the config-has-memory/wrapper-cannot case is owned by a FAKE engine in
# test_andes_sim_hvm_wiring.sh and needs no real engine here.
edit('tests/vsim/test_vsim_hvm_load.sh', [(
'''# --- Describe gating: hvm_size advertises the HVM TRANSPORT, so it must be
# non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_hvm/get_hvm backdoor
# pair (the ax46 F3 regression lesson: config has the memory, wrapper has no
# backdoor -> must report 0 or the driver would pass --hvm and load_image
# would throw). Field extraction rides the shared hybrid_describe_int.
if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)" != 262144 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_hvm_load]: premium --describe does not report hvm_size 262144"
  exit 1
fi
AX46="$(dirname "$VSIM_BIN")/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[vsim_hvm_load]: ax46 (no set_hvm/get_hvm backdoor) must describe hvm_size 0"
    exit 1
  fi
fi''',
'''# --- Describe gating: hvm_size advertises the HVM TRANSPORT (the wrapper's
# set_hvm/get_hvm backdoor), not merely the config's memory -- the driver
# reads it to decide whether to pass --hvm at all. The mismatched case
# (config has the memory, wrapper cannot reach it -> must report 0) is owned

if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)" != 262144 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_hvm_load]: premium --describe does not report hvm_size 262144"
  exit 1
fi''')])
edit('tests/vsim/test_vsim_lm_load.sh', [(
'''# --- Describe gating: ilm_size/dlm_size advertise the LM TRANSPORT, so they
# must be non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_ilm/set_dlm

# would pass --ilm/--dlm and load_image would throw (the F3 ax46 regression).
# Field extraction rides the shared hybrid_describe_int (paths.sh), so this
# asserts VALUES, not the descriptor's JSON formatting.
if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)" != 65536 ] \\
   || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)" != 32768 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"
  exit 1
fi
AX46="$(dirname "$VSIM_BIN")/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ] \\
     || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"
    exit 1
  fi
fi''',
'''# --- Describe gating: ilm_size/dlm_size advertise the LM TRANSPORT (the
# wrapper's set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor), not merely the config's memories -- the
# driver reads them to decide whether to pass --ilm/--dlm at all. The
# mismatched case (config has the memories, wrapper cannot reach them -> must
# report 0) is owned by test_andes_sim_hvm_wiring.sh with a FAKE engine, so it
# needs no second real engine here. Field extraction rides the shared
# hybrid_describe_int (paths.sh), so this asserts VALUES, not the descriptor's
# JSON formatting.
if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)" != 65536 ] \\
   || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)" != 32768 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"
  exit 1
fi''')])

# --- 4. hvm_wiring's real-engine consistency check -> the shipped 2nd engine

AX46="$BINDIR/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"''',
  '''# Real-engine consistency: whatever the SECOND shipped engine's OWN --describe

AX46="$BINDIR/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3"'''),

1 # hybrid_sim
   2 
   3 Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
   4 (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
   5 across a magic-CSR boundary.
   6 
   7 Submodule:
   8 
   9 - `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  10   contract under `include/hybrid/`, shared by the plugin, the driver, and vsim.
  11 
  12 QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries (set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` and
  13 `VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`; see `config.env.example`), not vendored as
  14 submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.
  15 
  16 ## Quickstart
  17 
  18 ```sh
  19 git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
  20 bash scripts/build_all.sh
  21 bash scripts/test_all.sh
  22 ```
  23 
  24 Subcommands: `run`, `profile`, `list`, `doctor`. Run `./andesim -h` for the
  25 full list. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` is the end-user guide: first runs on
  26 each model, then every `run` option one by one.
  27 `./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine <id>` prints the
  28 hybrid-supported guest memory map (USER_GUIDE section 5.5).
  29 
  30 ## Host dependencies
  31 
  32 - C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
  33 - Python 3
  34 - glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
  35 - pkg-config
  36 - a prebuilt `qemu-system-riscv64` (external; this repo no longer builds QEMU --
  37   set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`)
  38 - a prebuilt vsim (external; this repo no longer builds vsim -- set `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  39   in `config.env` to your vsim checkout's `build/` dir)
  40 
  41 ## Outputs
  42 
  43 After `bash scripts/build_all.sh`:
  44 
  45 - `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotIterationLoop.so`, the `andesim profile` plugin)
  46 
  47 QEMU and vsim are external prebuilt binaries: `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64`
  48 and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in `config.env`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Andes-CSR capability parity (the flywheel / drift guard).
#
# The offline deriver (scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py) computes, from a
# core's config.inc, which Andes CSRs it implements. The vsim
# engine compiles the SAME gate logic (src/hybrid/andes_caps*.hpp) and reports
# the list at runtime via `--describe` ("andes_csrs"). Fed the engine's OWN
# embedded build config.inc, the two must be byte-identical -- a disagreement
# means the resume/drain capability gate is wrong for that engine.
#
# Runs against EVERY built engine under $VSIM_BIN_DIR (each sim_* binary with
# a V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc beside it) -- a single hardcoded engine left
# new engines with zero parity coverage. Uses the engine's build config.inc
# (the exact blob the binary embeds), so offline and online share one source.
# The --describe half is opportunistic: it needs the engine rebuilt with the
# S3 describe change (a prebuilt binary that omits "andes_csrs" is skipped).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

DERIVE="$ROOT/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py"
[ -f "$DERIVE" ] || fail "missing deriver: $DERIVE"

VSIM_BIN_DIR="$(vsim_bin_dir)"

checked=0
for ENG in "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_*; do
  [ -x "$ENG" ] || continue
  name=$(basename "$ENG")            # sim_<engine>
  engine=${name#sim_}
  # The engine's embedded config.inc (copied next to its Verilated objects).
  CFG="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V$engine/obj_sc/config.inc"
  [ -f "$CFG" ] || fail "$name present but its build config.inc not found at $CFG"

  offline=$(python3 "$DERIVE" "$CFG") || fail "deriver failed on $CFG"
  [ -n "$offline" ] || fail "deriver produced an empty list for $CFG"

  online=$("$ENG" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin).get("andes_csrs", [])))' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$online" ]; then
    echo "[skip] $name --describe has no andes_csrs (rebuild vsim with the S3 change)"
    continue
  fi

input.command:
S=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/ce94e8da-4870-4504-9e19-bf6be936a80f/scratchpad; cat >| "$S/issue19.md" <<'MD'
## Decision (supersedes the original scope)

v0.1.0 ships **two** cycle-accurate engines, not one:

| Engine | VLEN/DLEN | ELEN | Caches | Privilege | QEMU pairing |
|--------|-----------|------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| `ax45mpv_premium` (default) | 512 | 32, no vector FP | 64 KB I$ / 8 KB D$ | M only | `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` |
| `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` | 1024 | 64, vector FP | 32 KB I$ / 32 KB D$ + 2 MB L3 | M/S/U | `-cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=1024` |

The vsim side builds only these two (its `config.yaml`). Every other CPU
config -- `ax45mpv_premium_full`, `ax45mpv_premium_max`, `ax46mpv_advanced`,
`ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw`, `d23`, `ax66_makatau` -- is deferred to a later
release.

Because `ax45mpv_premium` stays in the release, the two original requirements
about the environment check and the test-suite default are **moot**: both
already point at `ax45mpv_premium` and both already pass.

**S/U-privilege handoff is deferred, not validated.** The `rt_priv_smode` /
`rt_priv_umode` fixtures were pinned to the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau`, which
v0.1.0 does not ship, so they are out of the suite. Of the two shipped engines
`ax45mpv_premium` is M-mode-only (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) and can never
run them; `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` does carry all three levels, so re-enabling them
there -- paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` -- is the future work. The
fixture sources stay in `tests/fixtures/`.

## Required Behavior

* **The environment check reports success** on an install carrying the two
  shipped engines. (Already true: its default probe is `sim_ax45mpv_premium`.)
* **The e2e suite defaults to `ax45mpv_premium`** and passes. (Already true.)
* **No test pins an engine v0.1.0 does not ship.** A test that names a
  deferred engine hard-fails, or worse silently skips, on a correct install.
* **The engine release surface lives in ONE place**, so a future release
  changes one list instead of hunting through the harness.
* **S/U-privilege fixtures are out of the default suite**, and the docs say
  S/U handoff is unsupported in v0.1.0.
* Naming an engine explicitly must keep working, and an install that happens
  to carry another engine must still be able to run it.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: v0.1.0 engine release surface

  Scenario: Environment check passes on the shipped install
    Given an install carrying ax45mpv_premium and ax46mpv_fpga_l3
    When I run the environment check
    Then it reports success
    And it reports no failure about an absent engine

  Scenario: The test suite defaults to the shipped default engine
    Given an install carrying the two shipped engines
    When I run the end-to-end test suite without naming an engine
    Then the suite runs against "ax45mpv_premium"
    And the suite passes

  Scenario: No test depends on a deferred engine
    Given the harness scripts under tests/ and scripts/
    When I check them for engine names outside comments
    Then none of them names a deferred engine

  Scenario Outline: Both shipped engines are usable
    Given the cycle-accurate engine <engine>
    When I run the shipped runtime's syscall-window and gettimeofday fixtures
    Then both complete successfully

  Examples:
    | engine           |
    | ax45mpv_premium  |
    | ax46mpv_fpga_l3  |

  Scenario: S/U privilege is declared unsupported
    Given the v0.1.0 documentation
    Then it states S/U-privilege handoff is not supported
    And no privilege fixture runs in the default suite
```

## Delivery

vsim repo:

* `config.yaml` -- trimmed from 7 CPU configs to the two shipped ones.

andesim repo:

* `tests/lib/log.sh` -- new `shipped_cycle_engines()` /
  `deferred_cycle_engines()`: the single source of truth for the release
  surface.

  `ax66_makatau` the machine to itself; with the privilege fixtures gone the
  whole `SERIAL_RT_TESTS` / `SERIAL_PLAN` machinery is removed (-49/+13 lines).

---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS that page. Exactly 2G therefore
#           overflows and is rejected; 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that
#           fits. See driver/shm.cpp max_program_mem_bytes().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size stays a hidden alias of --mem-size.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"        # engine-portable (fast/cycle)
MELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"        # carries ROI markers (hybrid)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

require_driver
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"
[ -f "$MELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $MELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"

# hybrid <SIZE> <want-rc> then per-line assertions; runs the command ONCE.
hy() { "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --log-level 1 "$@" "$MELF" </dev/null 2>&1; }

# --- fast: pass-through to QEMU -m -------------------------------------------
# 1G accepted, program still runs.
expect 0 'hello from vplat' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 1G "$ELF"

1 // `andesim --version` -- the identity of every bundled component.
   2 //
   3 // AndeSim ships as four separately-built pieces: this driver, the shared ABI
   4 // headers it was compiled against, a QEMU binary, and a cycle-accurate engine
   5 // binary. An install can mix versions of them, so a bug report has to be able
   6 // to name all four.
   7 //
   8 // The two halves are versioned by different means, on purpose:
   9 //   * driver + ABI are built together, so their git identity is stamped into
  10 //     the binary at build time (cmake/build_stamp.cmake -> build_stamp.h);
  11 //   * QEMU and the engine arrive as PREBUILT binaries, so only the binaries
  12 //     themselves can say what they are -- they are asked at run time. A
  13 //     prebuilt binary can be older than the source tree it sits in, and that
  14 //     difference is exactly what this report exists to expose.
  15 //
  16 // This header is the pure core: the two output parsers and the renderer. The
  17 // collection side (git stamp + subprocess probes) lives in cmd_version.cpp.
  18 #ifndef ANDESIM_VERSION_HPP
  19 #define ANDESIM_VERSION_HPP
  20 
  21 #include <string>
  22 #include <string_view>
  23 #include <vector>

  28 // asked, or did not answer.

  30   std::string id;       // the engine id, e.g. "vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3"
  31   std::string version;  // what the binary reported, e.g. "87a0baa"
  32 };

  35 // that cannot be reached is reported, never dropped, and never fatal.

  38   std::string andesim;   // "<branch>/<short commit>" of the andesim checkout
  39   std::string abi;       // "<branch>/<short commit>" of the shared ABI headers

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash

   3 #
   4 # AndeSim is delivered as four separately-built pieces (driver, shared ABI
   5 # headers, QEMU binary, engine binary) whose versions can be mixed in one
   6 # install. This asserts that all four are reported, that the two PREBUILT ones
   7 # are read from the binaries actually in use (not recorded at build time -- a
   8 # prebuilt binary can be older than the source tree it sits in), and that an
   9 # unreachable component is reported "unknown" instead of failing the command.

  11 # The build-time half is cross-checked against git run independently here; the
  12 # run-time half is cross-checked against what the binaries themselves answer.

  14 # they are hermetic -- no real binary is moved or damaged.

  16 
  17 SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  18 ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  19 . "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
  20 
  21 require_driver
  22 
  23 # `--` so a pattern may start with a dash (e.g. the --version help line).

  25 
  26 TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
  27 
  28 # A fake engine: self-describes as cycle-accurate (so discovery keeps it) and
  29 # reports $1 as its own version, the way the real sim_* binaries do.
  30 make_fake_engine() {  # <path> <id> <version>
  31   cat >"$1" <<EOF
  32 #!/bin/sh
  33 [ "\$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}' && exit 0
  34 [ "\$1" = "--version" ] && printf 'Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation.\nVersion : $3\n' && exit 0
  35 exit 1
  36 EOF
  37   chmod +x "$1"
  38 }
  39 
  40 # 1. The command exists, exits 0, and carries one labelled line per component.
  41 V=$("$BIN" --version 2>&1); rc=$?
  42 [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--version rc=$rc want 0:"$'\n'"$V"
  43 has '^AndeSim ' "$V"  || fail "--version: no AndeSim line:"$'\n'"$V"
  44 has '^  abi '   "$V"  || fail "--version: no abi line:"$'\n'"$V"
  45 has '^  qemu '  "$V"  || fail "--version: no qemu line:"$'\n'"$V"
  46 has '^  engine ' "$V" || fail "--version: no engine line:"$'\n'"$V"
  47 ok "--version: exits 0 with an AndeSim / abi / qemu / engine line"
  48

  50 # + short commit of THIS checkout; the abi line carries the branch + short
  51 # commit of the shared ABI submodule. Both recorded here independently of the
  52 # driver, straight from git.

  54   local d="$1" b c
  55   c=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null) || return 1

  57     b=$(git -C "$d" describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2>/dev/null) ||

  64     fail "--version: AndeSim line should read 'vX.Y.Z ($AS_ID)':"$'\n'"$V"
  65   has "^  abi +$ABI_ID$" "$V" ||
  66     fail "--version: abi line should read '$ABI_ID':"$'\n'"$V"

  69   echo "[skip] git identity cross-check: not a git checkout"
  70 fi
  71 
  72 # 3. Run-time half, QEMU: the reported number is what the QEMU binary in use
  73 # says about itself, asked here directly.
  74 QEMU=$(qemu_bin)

  76   QV=$("$QEMU" --version 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*version \([0-9][^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)

  78   has "^  qemu +$QV$" "$V" || fail "--version: qemu line should read '$QV':"$'\n'"$V"

  85 # use says about itself. Pinned to ONE real engine via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR so
  86 # the expected line is unambiguous.

  91   mkdir -p "$TMP/one"; ln -sf "$SIM" "$TMP/one/sim_pinned"

  96   has "^  engine +$EV$" "$E" ||

  98   ok "--version: engine = $EV (cross-checked against $SIM itself)"

 101   # build and so reports the same commit, that value is stated ONCE. Eight
 102   # identical lines would be noise.
 103   [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -c '^  engine ')" -eq 1 ] ||
 104     fail "--version: engines agreeing on a version must collapse to one line:"$'\n'"$V"
 105   has "^  engine +$EV$" "$V" ||
 106     fail "--version: the single engine line should read '$EV':"$'\n'"$V"
 107   ok "--version: all real engines agree -> the commit is reported once, unadorned"
 108 else
 109   echo "[skip] engine cross-check: no $SIM"
 110 fi
 111 
 112 # 5. The engine value follows the BINARY, not any build-time record: swapping
 113 # in a binary that reports a different version changes the line, nothing else.
 114 mkdir -p "$TMP/a" "$TMP/b"
 115 make_fake_engine "$TMP/a/sim_fake" "verilator:fakecfg" "87a0baa"
 116 make_fake_engine "$TMP/b/sim_fake" "verilator:fakecfg" "9b01c20"
 117 A=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/a" "$BIN" --version 2>&1)
 118 B=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/b" "$BIN" --version 2>&1)
 119 has '^  engine +87a0baa$' "$A" || fail "engine line A:"$'\n'"$A"
 120 has '^  engine +9b01c20$' "$B" || fail "engine line B:"$'\n'"$B"
 121 ok "--version: the engine line follows the binary in use (87a0baa -> 9b01c20)"
 122

 124 # visible: one line per DISTINCT version, each naming which engines report it
 125 # (grouped by version, not by engine).
 126 mkdir -p "$TMP/both"
 127 make_fake_engine "$TMP/both/sim_one" "verilator:one" "87a0baa"
 128 make_fake_engine "$TMP/both/sim_two" "verilator:two" "9b01c20"
 129 make_fake_engine "$TMP/both/sim_three" "verilator:three" "87a0baa"
 130 M=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/both" "$BIN" --version 2>&1)
 131 [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep -c '^  engine ')" -eq 2 ] ||
 132   fail "--version: expected one line per distinct version:"$'\n'"$M"
 133 has '^  engine +87a0baa \(vsim:one, vsim:three\)$' "$M" || fail "mixed install, 87a0baa group:"$'\n'"$M"
 134 has '^  engine +9b01c20 \(vsim:two\)$' "$M" || fail "mixed install, 9b01c20 group:"$'\n'"$M"
 135 ok "--version: a mixed install stays visible, grouped by version"
 136 
 137 # 6b. Engines that agree collapse to one unadorned line, however many there are.
 138 mkdir -p "$TMP/agree"
 139 make_fake_engine "$TMP/agree/sim_one" "verilator:one" "87a0baa"
 140 make_fake_engine "$TMP/agree/sim_two" "verilator:two" "87a0baa"
 141 make_fake_engine "$TMP/agree/sim_three" "verilator:three" "87a0baa"
 142 G=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/agree" "$BIN" --version 2>&1)
 143 [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$G" | grep -c '^  engine ')" -eq 1 ] ||
 144   fail "--version: agreeing engines must collapse to one line:"$'\n'"$G"
 145 has '^  engine +87a0baa$' "$G" || fail "agreeing engines:"$'\n'"$G"
 146 ok "--version: engines that agree report the commit once, with no id suffix"
 147 
 148 # 7. A component that cannot be reached is still reported, clearly marked
 149 # unknown, and the command still exits 0 -- engine gone, then QEMU gone.
 150 mkdir -p "$TMP/empty"

 179

content.text:
因為 `list engines` 是**動態掃目錄**的：`engine_registry.cpp` 掃 `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` 底下所有 `sim_*` 檔案，誰在就列誰。

我改的 `config.yaml` 只決定**以後 build 出什麼**，不會刪掉已經 build 好的檔案。你的 build dir 裡舊的 binary 全都還在：

```
sim_ax45mpv_premium              ← 出貨
sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3              ← 出貨
sim_ax45mpv_premium_full         ← 已 deferred，檔案還在
sim_ax45mpv_premium_max          ← 同上
sim_ax46mpv_advanced             ← 同上
sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw  ← 同上
sim_ax66_makatau                 ← 同上
sim_d23                          ← rv32，discovery 會跳過（所以沒列出來）
sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.biu32-backup ← 備份檔
```

這其實是 #19 講的正確行為：「裝了額外 engine 的人還是可以用 `--engine` 跑它」。但如果你要看到「真正 v0.1.0 install 的樣子」（只有 2 顆），要把多的 binary 移走。

我**不建議直接刪** —— 每顆重 build 都要跑 Verilator 很久。要的話我幫你搬到 `build/deferred/`，隨時搬回來：

```sh
mkdir -p /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/deferred
mv .../build/sim_{ax45mpv_premium_full,ax45mpv_premium_max,ax46mpv_advanced,ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw,ax66_makatau,d23} \
   .../build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.biu32-backup \
   .../build/deferred/
```

encodes the 16 GiB rule; only this shell contract still asserted the old one,
and had been failing since.

is paid for), and 2047M still flat from zero.

## Problem

`--runtime linux` rejects a too-large `--mem-size` with this message:

```
--mem-size 17G exceeds what --runtime linux can address (max 16G, the AE350
DRAM + DRAM_EXT windows; hybrid mode has its own 2G cap)
```

The last clause is **wrong**. U10f moved hybrid onto the same contiguous high
view -- `max_program_mem_bytes()` is now the 16 GiB DRAM + DRAM_EXT windows
minus the one reserved V-scratch page -- so hybrid has no separate 2 GiB cap.
A user reading this message would size a hybrid run to 2G believing that is
the ceiling, when 2G is merely where the map switches to the high view at
`0x8_00000000`.

The same retired claim survives in two comments next to code that already
implements the 16 GiB rule:

* `driver/cmd_run.cpp` -- "the usable --mem-size is 2 GiB minus that page",
  directly above the `mem > max_program_mem_bytes()` check
* `driver/infra_test.cpp` -- "Hybrid keeps its own separate 2 GiB cap in
  cmd_run"

## Required Behavior

* **The `--runtime linux` ceiling message must not attribute a 2 GiB cap to
  hybrid mode.** It may state its own 16 GiB ceiling; it must not describe
  hybrid's as different.
* Comments that describe the cap must match the code they sit next to.
* The ceiling itself does not change: 16 GiB accepted, more rejected, and the
  flag plus the runtime are still named in the message.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin

    Given the fast model with "--runtime linux"
    When I ask for a --mem-size above the addressable window
    Then the error names the flag, the 16G ceiling and the runtime
    And it does not claim hybrid mode is capped at 2G

  Scenario: The ceiling is unchanged
    Given the fast model with "--runtime linux"
    Then 16G is accepted
    And 17G is rejected
```

## QA Procedure

1. Run a `--runtime linux` fast run with `--mem-size 17G`. Read the message:
   it must name the flag, 16G and the runtime, and say nothing about a 2 GiB
   hybrid cap.
2. Repeat with `--mem-size 16G`: accepted.
3. Read the two comments above; each must describe the 16 GiB rule.

fix(driver): the linux mem-size error no longer claims a 2G hybrid cap (behavioral)

U10f put hybrid on the same contiguous high view -- max_program_mem_bytes() is
the 16 GiB DRAM + DRAM_EXT windows minus the reserved V-scratch page -- so the
"hybrid mode has its own 2G cap" clause in --runtime linux's ceiling message
became false. A user who believed it would size a hybrid run to 2G thinking
that was the ceiling, when 2G is merely where the map switches to the high
view at 0x8_00000000. The clause is dropped; the 16 GiB ceiling it reports is
unchanged, and the message still names the flag and the runtime.

The same retired claim is corrected in the two comments that sat next to code
already implementing the 16 GiB rule (cmd_run.cpp's early cap, infra_test's
preamble). A test pins the message against the regression.

Closes #27

    run --mode fast --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium vplat_hello.elf   rc=0, \"hello from vplat\"
